page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and utilizing a KVM hypervisor. Network connectivity is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance divergence between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Single-threaded gzip compression also registers in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by middle-tier results in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average read and write speeds, although the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density of 8.0 GB per core, the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not demand high single-thread compute performance. The lack of local storage requires architectural planning for external storage latency. This profile is suited for memory-intensive applications such as database operations, Redis caching layers, and multi-threaded text or image processing. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or high-performance computing workloads that require high clock speeds or local NVMe storage.
